% Numbers computed from results/*.csv; do not edit by hand.

\paragraph{Controlled cross-client sharing}
We isolate the effect of sharing experiences across clients on a single topic, MMLU High School
Geography, holding the evaluation conditions fixed. The frozen repository contains 6{,}000 distilled
experiences contributed by four clients, exactly 25 per construction question per client. Three
candidate pools are compared. \emph{Local-only} exposes the requesting client's own 1{,}500 experiences;
\emph{Shared-matched} exposes a 1{,}500-entry pool drawn evenly from all four clients (375 each, 25 per
construction question); \emph{Shared-full} exposes all 6{,}000. The matched pool is rebuilt
independently from three preselected seeds (20261103, 20261104, 20261105) and the same pool serves every
request. Each of the 55 unseen questions is answered ten times by the requesting client's assigned
identity, with BM25 retrieval of the top five experiences and identical model, prompt and decoding
settings across pools; only the retrievable set differs. Accuracy is averaged over questions, and
confidence intervals come from a paired bootstrap that resamples the 55 question keys.

\paragraph{Results}
Local-only reaches 80.36\% (95\% CI [70.73, 88.37]), Shared-matched 80.24\% ([71.39, 88.18]) and
Shared-full 78.18\% ([69.27, 86.55]). Mixing experiences from the four clients therefore does not change
accuracy at a matched candidate count: the paired difference is $-0.12$ percentage points
([-3.03, +2.73]). Expanding the matched pool to the full 6{,}000 experiences likewise shows no gain;
the difference is $-2.06$ percentage points ([-6.18, +2.00]) and the overall full-versus-local gap is
$-2.18$ points ([-6.55, +2.18]). The three matched pools individually score 79.27\%, 82.00\% and
79.45\%, so the pool-to-pool spread is comparable to the differences between policies. All intervals
include zero, so within this controlled setting the measured accuracy is consistent with the local
baseline; the experiment does not support a claim that cross-client sharing improves accuracy, nor that
it degrades it.
